root_idea.summary: The root denotes despairing of something: giving up hope in it, especially hope of good or divine mercy.
root_idea.development: The core despair sense appears in the Form I verb and its participial derivatives. Classical Arabic also extends it to a causative Form II meaning “to make someone despair” and an intensive adjectival form meaning “intensely despairing,” while recording a separate noun use for withholding.

senses.definition: To despair of something; to give up hope of good or mercy.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction uses مِنْ for what is despaired of, especially divine mercy or good. Reported vocalic and dialectal variants of the Form I verb do not create additional senses.

senses.definition: Despairing; one who has given up hope of good.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle, occurring in the Quran in the plural قَانِطِينَ; in its cited construction it denotes those who despair and are told not to do so.
A Quranic nominal/adjectival characterization treated lexically as an intensive counterpart of قَانِط. The cited verse places it in a paired description with يَؤُوسٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Withholding or debarring; specifically, withholding one's water from others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct Classical noun use, as in withholding water from someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to despair; to make someone give up hope.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive causative Form II construction, including causing people to despair of God's mercy.
A Classical adjectival form treated alongside قَانِط; it is distinct in form from the supplied Quranic active-participle group.
